prose.text: Offers sporadic (chartered) service from [[London]] and [[Dublin]]. Direct flights from Singapore, Bangkok, Sharjah, Muscat and [[Dubai]] are also available. Jaipur also has daily domestic air links with many Indian cities such as [[Jodhpur]], [[Udaipur]], [[Aurangabad]], [[Delhi]], [[Hyderabad]], [[Kolkata]], [[Goa]], [[Chennai]], [[Ahmedabad]], [[Bangalore]], [[Mumbai]], [[Pune]] and [[Indore]].

name: Amber Fort
directions: 11 km North of central Jaipur, local bus #5 from Hawa Mahal or New Gate
price: ₹100/20 for Indian adult/student and ₹500/100 for foreign adult/student. Included in the '''Composite Ticket'''. There is a special evening viewing from 6:30-9AM, ₹100 for all, Composite Ticket not valid. Camera: free. Audioguides ₹200. Elephant rides: ₹1100. Consider not taking elephant rides as there have been many reports of these animals not being kept and cared for in humane ways

prose.text: This massive fort-palace complex built in hybrid Hindu-Muslim style dates back to Raja Man Singh and was the royal palace of the Kachwahas from c. 1600-1727. It's one of six [[UNESCO World Heritage]] forts in Rajasthan. The name has nothing to do with the rather pretty pastel yellow colour; instead, the fort is named after the area of Amber, in turn named after the goddess Amba.
A palace adorned with thousands on thousands of mirror tiles on the walls and ceiling.

name: Jaigarh Fort
directions: A 1 km walk uphill from '''Amber Fort''', or ₹100/200 for motorbike/auto-rickshaw
price: ₹35/100 for Indian/foreigner. Camera: ₹50 (if you do not disclose that you have a camera and later the police/their person sees you talking a photo (e.g. with your phone) they may ask you to show your ticket, and if you don't have one, will either ask you to buy the ₹50 ticket or penalise you). Video ₹200. Automobile ₹50

prose.text: Never conquered in battle, this was considered the strongest of the three forts in the area. It is best-known as the site of the world's largest cannon, the ''Jaivana'', which was test-fired only once — according to legend, despite using only the half the design amount of gunpowder, the cannonball flew {{km|35}}! A better reason to visit the fort, though, are the scenic gardens at the other end and the spectacular views over the Amber Fort and the hills around. The remains of the foundry where the Jaivana (and many more) were cast are also in the fort grounds. There are multiple boards with "no tips allowed," in case someone is bothering you.

name: Nahargarh Fort
price: ₹50/200 for Indians/foreigners. Included in the 5-monument Composite Ticket. ₹400/₹700 (Indian/foreigners) for the tour of the Wax Museum and the Sheesh Mahal.

prose.text: The smallest of the three forts, notable primarily for excellent views over Man Sagar lake and the vast sprawl of Jaipur. Built in 1734 by the Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in a mix of Indian and European styles, the fort also houses the (relatively) compact Madhavendra Bhawan palace, although its former splendour is fading under layers of graffiti and pigeon droppings. Some of the film ''Rang De Basanti'' were shot at this fort. To get to the area where the "Pathshala" song was shot, take a left turn as soon as you enter the fort. An autorickshaw can be taken from the stand in front of the Amber fort. The fort also houses the Jaipur's Wax Museum and Sheesh Mahal, although tickets for these have to be bought separately and are ridiculously expensive. Beware if buying the Wax Museum and Sheesh Mahal combo ticket, you'll be paraded through the largely unimpressive museum and then be told to queue for the Sheesh Mahal which can last from 30 minutes to 2 hours.

name: City Palace
directions: Inside the old city, close to New Gate and Hawa Mahal, metro: {{station|Badi Chaupar|pink}}
price: ₹400 for Indians, ₹1200 for foreigners, half price(₹200/₹600) for students, children below 12, Indian senior citizens and Indian defense personnel; a composite ticket (₹500/₹300) for Indians (₹1700/₹850) for foreigners gives extra access to Jaigarh Fort and Royal Cenotaphs

prose.text: An imposing blend of traditional Rajput and Mughal architecture. It is a vast palace complex occupying nearly one-seventh of the Pink City. It was built by Maharaja Jai Singh II. The complex is divided into a series of courtyards, sprawling gardens and buildings. It is home to several palatial structures like the '''Chandra Mahal''', (home to present Maharajah of Jaipur), '''Mubarak Mahal''' (housing a textile museum), '''Diwan-e-Khas''' (or Hall of Private audience housing the two largest silver vessels in the world, which are duly mentioned in the Guinness book), the '''Diwan-e-Aam''' ( or Hall of Public Audience) and the gateway '''Ridhi Sidhi Pol''' (with four small doorways decorated with motifs depicting the four seasons). Be warned that although they sell tickets for taking photos with a camera inside, most exhibits inside have a "no photography" sign.

name: Hawa Mahal
price: ₹10 for Indians, ₹200 for foreigners. Included in the Composite Ticket, free on 18 May. Camera free
commons_image: East facade Hawa Mahal Jaipur from ground level (July 2022) - img 01.jpg

prose.text: Built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Singh as part of City Palace, it was an extension of the ''Zenana'' (women's) chamber. Its purpose was to allow royal ladies to observe everyday life in the street below without being seen. It is a five storey high red sandstone structure complete with over 950 windows. The breeze (or hawa in Hindi) circulates through these windows, giving the palace its name. The iconic facade is best seen from the street, which is free.

name: Jal Mahal
directions: on the way to Amer Road
price: Free to view and photograph, but as of 2015, it is private property, so you probably won't be allowed to enter

prose.text: This beautiful Jal Mahal or water palace was made by the King of Amber in the middle of the Man Sagar Lake. The Jal Mahal represents the use of Mughal and Rajput architecture style.
A 450-year-old palace, built around 1550 by Jaswant Singh.

name: Birla Mandir (aka The Marble Temple)
directions: below the well-known Moti Dungri Fort

prose.text: This is a relatively new temple made of white marble with beautiful carvings. It covers a vast area in Jaipur city and is built in a contemporary manner. Birla Temple is completely constructed with the finest high-quality white marbles. In addition to having statues and paintings of Hindu deities, the temple has pictures of famous philosophers from around the world including Socrates, Confucius and Zoroaster. No bags (besides purses), food, cameras. No photos allowed in the temple, but rules are not enforced outside.

name: Galtaji
address: 10 km from Jaipur on Jaipur-Agra highway near Sisodia Rani Garden

prose.text: An ancient Hindu pilgrimage site. The main temple, Galtaji, is constructed in pink stone. The temple has a number of pavilions with rounded roofs, exquisitely carved pillars and painted walls. The temple is surrounded by natural springs and reservoirs that are considered holy. There are also seven tanks or ''kunds'' here. There are two routes to reach the temple: if you arrive from west you will have to hike uphill and downhill for about 20 minutes; the eastern gate is easily accessible by car, though it is a longer journey to get there.

name: Galwar Bagh
directions: adjacent to Suriya Mandir (aka The Sun Temple)

prose.text: Locals and tourists come here to feed the surprisingly tame monkeys, use the temples, and enjoy the views. You can climb to the top of the hill and then down into the valley to see the Monkey Temple, while enjoying the company of countless monkeys, goats and other animals. At the top of the hill, you turn right to reach the Sun Temple for one of the best views of the city, especially at sunset. Monkey food is available for purchase at the bottom of the hill. Entrance to the temples are free, but local religious people may ask for donations and there is a ₹50 charge for using a camera.

For Vaishnavites, particularly followers of Lord Krishna, this is the most important temple in the world after Vrindavan. Lord Krishna presiding in the temple were brought to Jaipur from Vrindavan during Mughal rein. According to popular legend, Lord Krishna's idol in the temple looks exactly like Krishna's form while his incarnation of Earth. It is at Jainiwas Gardens, Jalebi Chowk, in the same campus as City Palace. The temple was constructed in 1590.

A 17th-century Hindu temple, and one of the few in India where Meera Bai, the poet-saint of the Bhakti movement, is enshrined alongside Lord Krishna. It is also a site of cultural interest during festivals like Janmashtami, where devotees gather in large numbers for special darshan and bhajans dedicated to Krishna and Meera.

Jain temple in Shivdaspura, well known as “Bara Padampura”, famous in north India for its very beautiful statue of God Padamprabhu (The 6th Teerthankar for Jains). God is sitting in a crossed leg seating posture. The statue is 0.7 m high and made of pure white stone. It was found while digging for foundation of a house.

name: Moti Dungri Mandir
commons_image: Jaipur - Sri Moti Dungri Ganesh Ji Mandir (2022) - img 01.jpg

prose.text: This temple, dedicated to Lord Ganesha, is the main centre of religion for Jaipur people. Moti Dungri, meaning Pearl Hill, is a small hill that hosts a temple and a palace. It is said that this temple was built before construction of the rest of the city was begun, so as to protect the city.

name: Shri Digamber Jain Atishya Kshetra Mandir, Sanghiji

prose.text: A popular Jain temple.

name: Gaitore
directions: in the walled city area named Brahmpuri, the foothills of Nahargarh Fort

prose.text: A royal cremation site of the rulers of Jaipur.

name: Iswari Minar Swarga Sal
directions: look for the tall tower near Tripolia Gate; the entrance is not from the main street, but is around the back of the shops; you can get there from the alley that’s 50 m west of the minaret along Chandpol Bazaar, there's also an entrance near the City Palace, which is 50 m west of Tripolia Gate and 200 m east of the minaret

prose.text: A minaret with great views of Jaipur. There is an alternative to the minaret that's open 24/7. Just across the other side of the road (Chandpol Bazaar) from the minaret is a shopping complex with stairs up to a rooftop area where you can get basically the same view as from the minaret. To get there, go through the arched gateway almost opposite the minaret, then as soon as you get to the courtyard, look to the left for a metal spiral staircase and keep climbing until you reach the roof, walk around the corridor to the next set of stair and go up another floor until you know you can't go any higher.

name: Jantar Mantar
directions: very close to the City Palace.

prose.text: This [[UNESCO World Heritage site|UNESCO world heritage site]] is the largest of five astronomical observatories build by Maharaja Jai Singh during the period 1727-1734 in Northern India. The observatory consists of fourteen major geometric devices (or ''yantra'' in Hindi) for measuring time, predicting eclipses, tracking stars in their orbits, ascertaining the declinations of planets and determining the celestial altitudes etc. There is signage providing elaborate explanations for the use of each device, and guides can be hired to provide much the same information in a more digestible format. Guides' charge is 200 rupees for 4 people. For a better explanation, you can take a guide. The audio guide at the observatory isn't great and doesn't tell you very much more information than the already existent signs. The observatory, the water and the wind palace are free on 18 May.

name: Panna Meena Ka Kund Stepwell
directions: near Anokhi Museum and Amber Fort

prose.text: People come here to get water, swim or hang out with their loved ones.
Built in 1868 by Maharaja Sawai Ram Singh of Jaipur, this garden contains a bird park, zoo, Ravindra Rang Manch Theatre, art gallery, exhibition ground, gymnasium and several cafes and picnic spots.

This palace was established by Sawai Jai Singh for his queen Sisodia, rulers of one of the oldest kingdoms of India. There are tiered multi-level gardens with fountains, watercourses and painted pavilions. A double-storeyed palace occupies the top terrace of the garden. The palace has many galleries, pavilions and beautiful murals depicting scenes from the life of lord Krishna.
The garden is a real treat for those who want to see a fusion of Mughal and Hindu culture.
In the serene environment of Ram Niwas Bagh, this garden is prized for its rich flora and fauna.
A wildlife sanctuary on the Aravalli Hills. It is home to species like leopards, sloth bears, wild boars, jackals, hyenas, peacocks, owls, eagles, and various species of snakes and frogs.
Another leopard sanctuary on the Jaipur Ridge.

A large traffic circle with one of the biggest circular parks in India. Built by the Jaipur Development Authority (JDA), it is one of Jaipur's popular leisure destinations, close to the airport. There are multiple concentric tracks in the park, surrounded by rose gardens. The '''Patrika Gate''' may look like a Rajput-era structure, even though it was built in 2016.

A beautiful clean museum dedicated to the traditional art of hand block printing textiles, this museum is housed in a restored heritage haveli tucked into the back streets of old Amber. Small cafe (see "Eat"), clean toilets, small shop selling hand printed contemporary wearable clothes and textiles, friendly staff and a printer and block carver demonstrating their crafts every day.

name: Albert Hall Museum
price: ₹40/300 for Indians/foreigners. ₹20/150 for Indian/non-Indian students. Students must carry their student identity cards.Included in the 5-monument ''Composite Ticket''

prose.text: A fine example of Indo-Saracenic architecture, this building was designed by Sir Samuel Swinton Jacob and was opened as public museum in 1887. Maharaja Ram Singh wanted this building to be a town hall, but his successor, Madho Singh II, decided it should be a museum for the art of Jaipur and included as part of the new Ram Nivas Garden. The museum has a rich collection of artefacts like paintings, carpets, ivory, stone, metal sculptures and colourful crystal works. It is named after King Edward VII (Albert Edward), during whose visit to the city as the Prince of Wales, its foundation stone was laid on 6 February 1876.

A jewellery museum, with a collection of 4000 objects. Over 800 objects are displayed over two floors while the remaining objects are kept in visual storage. The museum has fine jewellery, hand-crafted antiques, and exquisite curios to showcase the craftsmanship and rich tradition of Indian jewellery. Several different types of Indian jewellery at the museum constitute a visual representation of history of art and process of jewellery making.[2] The collection ranges from tribal jewellery, in wood and metal, to silver and gold pieces. It is an extensive collection that shows how the traditional craftsmanship has impacted modern and contemporary design sensibilities.

name: Statue Circle
directions: intersection of Bhagwan Das Rd and Prithviraj Rd

prose.text: Statue Circle is exactly what it sounds like: a roundabout that contains a statue that is beautifully lit up at night. It is the life-size statue of the Great Ruler and Founder of Jaipur, Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II

The seat of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha). The building was built in 1994-2001 to replace the Sawai Man Singh Town Hall as the seat of the legislature. The exterior features jharokhas, chhatris, Kamanis, baradaris, arches, todis, etc., all examples of traditional Rajasthani architecture.

name: Amber Fort Sound and Light Show

prose.text: Experience the history, culture and life of Amber through this spectacular show. Amitabh Bachhan narrates the story of Rajasthani kings with a script written by Gulzar. Don't forget the mosquito repellent. The light show can be watched from outside the fort, but the sound won't be audible from there. There is also a sound and light show at Jantar Mantar for ₹100.
With a capacity of 30,000, this hosts the Rajasthan team and Rajathan Royals in IPL.

name: B.M. Birla Auditorium and Conference Hall
address: Birla Institute of Scientific Research, Statue Circle

prose.text: These are at the heart of Jaipur. This auditorium is spread over 9.8 acres and includes a computer centre, interactive science museum, an information processing centre, library, a processing planetarium, eight research divisions, a dissemination cell and an auditorium. The auditorium has a seating capacity of 1,350 and is among the largest in India. This auditorium is built up to international conference standards. However, people visiting Jaipur for leisure are likely to be most interested in the [http://www.bisr.res.in/planetarium.php Planetarium] (all shows in Hindi) or [http://www.bisr.res.in/museum.php Science Museum] (under renovation as of November 2015) that are part of the complex.

name: Rajmandir Cinema
address: C-16, Panch Batti, Bhagwan Das Rd, C-Scheme

prose.text: An experience in itself, and another "don't miss". Once known as the best cinema India, and still the best in Rajasthan, it offers an overwhelming experience. From the pushing, shoving, and general chaos in the ticket queue, to an audience that laughs, cries, cheers, claps, and consistently talks through the entire film, the Rajmandir provides an insight into Rajasthani culture. The films can be interesting; ''Masala'' movies are action, drama, mystery, suspense, and epics all wrapped into one single film, teeming with dances and obligatory wet sari scenes, and unabashedly lifting generous amounts of plot devices from Western films. The theatre-goers are very friendly and genuinely curious about overseas visitors who come to the Raj. Don't be put off by "House Full" notices at the entrance. The box office opens again a nominal 45 minutes before the next performance, and there are usually tickets available. Box seats at ₹120 go first, so it's worth going early to avoid disappointment. Shows at 12:30PM, 3:30PM, 6:30PM and 9:30PM. A great place to meet locals, with the nearby McDonald's as a central congregation spot.

name: Heiwa Heaven The Resort
address: Jaisinghpura Khor, Jamdoli Chauraha, Agra Rd

prose.text: Heiwa Heaven is a Jaipur-based luxury resort that hosts parties and destination weddings.

The largest park in Jaipur, at the middle of the city. A big lush green beautiful garden and Rambagh Polo Ground and golf club nearby makes it an enjoyable place. The park also has a {{km|4}} long jogging and walking track. A number of migratory and native birds visit the park during the year. Furthermore, there's a {{ft|269}} tall flag of India flying at the middle, one of the largest in India.

A popular destination among bird enthusiasts, with about 150 bird species flock around the eastern side of the dam every year, including the uncommon lesser whistling-duck and the widespread eastern cattle egret.

name: Chokhi Dhani
price: Traditional Rajasthani dining: Adult: ₹700; Kids up to 3.5 feet high: ₹350; AC Royal Rajasthani Dining: Adult: ₹900; Kids up to 3.5 feet high: ₹500; Multicuisine buffet: Adult: ₹950; Children up to 1 m tall: ₹650. Rooms: ₹5999-34999/night per double room

prose.text:
Around 18 km from Central Jaipur on the Jaipur-[[Tonk]] highway, Chokhi Dhani (''Fine Hamlet'' in Rajasthani dialect) is a kind of virtual village and also a 5-star resort. There are lodging facilities available, but the real attraction is the evening fun-fairs. There are two excellent places to enjoy Rajasthani food served in the traditional mode at their resort. Chokhi Dhani a.k.a. Lalten Restaurant is a more popular place because it is on the main road near the airport and also has other attractions, such as horseback riding, camel riding, bullock cart rides, a maze, boating and kathputli (puppet) shows. You can also watch live folk dances and listen to live folk music for free. It gives the visitor a glimpse of culture from different parts of Rajasthan, and could be nice if you will not have time to see much of Rajasthan yourself. It opens at 5PM, and be sure to get there early as many of the sites are difficult to see when it gets dark. It's a 30-min rickshaw ride from Central Jaipur, or you can go there by bus or taxi, but you are best off making sure you have a ride back.
Consider buying the pass for AC hall, because the outdoor seating is a self-served buffet, while in the AC Dining you'll be served food. This makes a massive difference when there are too many people at the restaurant, as the restaurant is unable to keep up with the demand for buffet food.
If you would prefer to sleep at the resort, [https://chokhidhani.com/ethnic-resort-jaipur/ have a look at their accommodation]. Avoid going there during the rainy season.

name: Dhamma Thali Vipassana Meditation Centre
address: There are 8 locations in Jaipur, which you can see [http://www.thali.dhamma.org/courses.shtml here], along with contact information of instructors

prose.text: 1- to 45-day meditation courses (10-day residential courses are given for new students) run for a donation.
Free hatha yoga courses from 6-7AM.

name: Maharaja Sawai Mansingh Sangeet Mahavidyalaya
opening_hours: Music lessons 8-11AM. Dance lessons, cultural exchange program, volunteer program and elephant care program, 4-8PM
price: Tuition started from ₹500/month a few years ago; their website gives no pricing, so contact them for further information

name: Nad Sadhna
address: E-122(A) Kataria Colony, Ram Nagar Extension

prose.text: An institute of Rajasthani music that holds group classes for vocals, guitars, synthesiser, tabla, sitar, flute, mouthorgan, dholak and dance. Tablas and sitars can be provided to students; other instruments must be brought by students to the class.
Bapu and Nehru bazaars are for budget and traditional shoppers. They are popular and chaotic bazaars selling many different items ranging from handicrafts to western outfits.

Johari bazaar and Chameliwala Market both best known as jewellery bazaars. There are hundreds of shops lined up in each bazaar selling jewellery of all types. Local jewellery along with authentic gems and stones can also be purchased.
Sweets for chamcham, also baked sweets and crispy samosas.
A popular ice-cream parlor on MI Rd. An assortment of ice cream shakes, and some indigenous ice cream flavours. Excellent after a hearty meal at one of the MI Rd restaurants.

name: Zolocrust
address: Hotel Clarks Amer, Jawaharlal Nehru Marg, Near Malviya Nagar

prose.text: The gourmet bakery and Italian restaurant is operated by chefs of Hotel Clarks Amer and serves exquisite bakery items, it also serves vegan and vegetarian food.

name: Anokhi Cafe
address: 2nd Floor, KK Square, C-11 Prithviraj Road
price: Salads: ₹120-200; sandwiches and savoury dishes: ₹150-300; desserts: ₹80-230; beverages: ₹25-250

prose.text: Mostly organic non-Indian-style ("international flavour") home-style cakes, freshly prepared sandwiches, pastries, savoury snacks plus organic coffee and a selection of good teas. Quiet, relaxing, good value for money, situated outside the Anokhi shop (see Anokhi Museum of Hand Printing listing in "See").

name: Ambrosia
address: In the Hotel Ramsingh Palace, B 2, Hathi Babau Ka Bagh, Kanti Nagar, Banipark

prose.text: Serving vegetarian and vegan, Chinese food and barbecue atop a 100-foot-high building providing a breathtaking view of the city.
Various chicken and mutton dishes for take-away.

name: Peacock Rooftop Restaurant
price: Soups and salads: ₹95-195; Tandoori starters: ₹245-495; Vegetarian mains: ₹185-325; Non-veg mains: ₹295-615; Continental cuisine: ₹295-395; etc

prose.text: A rooftop restaurant serving Indian, Western and Chinese food. Fast service and good value.
Simple place for lassis, snacks and breakfast. Claiming to be the oldest lasso place in Jaipur.

name: Rawat Mishthan Bhandar
address: Opposite Polo Victory Cinema, Station Road, Sindhi Camp
directions: Very close to railway station and bus stand
price: Nothing on the menu costs more than ₹250, including thalis, except for a special ₹450 tasting menu

prose.text: Do not miss the famous Pyaz ki Kachori, a spicy onion dish. Also, the ghewar and mawa kachori is famous.

name: Apno Gaon
address: 14, New Loha Mandi, Sikar Road, Vishwakarma Industrial Area

prose.text: Vegetarian food, including fresh vegetables and fruits. Slightly away from the main city: One has to go on a bumpy ride to reach there.
Indian and Chinese food, among the most popular vegetarian restaurants in Jaipur.

name: Handi Restaurant
address: Maya Mansion, Opp GPO, MI Rd

prose.text: Specialising in meat dishes; chicken, mutton, kebab, tandoori and the super spicy Rajasthani speciality lal maas.

name: Little Italy
address: C/11, K.K. Square, Prithviraj Marg, C-Scheme
price: pizzas and pastas are mostly in the ₹300-500 range

prose.text: Part of a chain with restaurants around India and some other Asian countries, as the name reveals, this is a place to go to for Italian food. Wide selection of pizza, pasta and other typical Italian food, also some Mexican dishes. Large range of wines.

name: LMB
price: Snacks, sandwiches, pizza: ₹50-310; breakfasts are mostly ₹130-280; lunch and dinner mains: ₹190-430; sweets: ₹60-200

prose.text: Good mid-range north Indian vegetarian restaurant. The restaurant sells good sweets and chat, Indian sweet and savory snacks, and is most famous for its Aloo ki Tikiya and Paneer Ghewar.

This is the house of a Royal Family in Civil Lines. Primarily a hotel, but they also serve food. You can call in advance and request a special dinner. Otherwise, dinners are served for in-house guests.

name: Mamu's Infusion
address: 101, 1st Floor, Mangalam Ambition Tower, Subhash Marg, C Scheme
price: Starters: ₹180-425; soup: ₹170-190; salad: ₹210-295; pizza: ₹370-450; pasta: ₹350-475; risotto: ₹320-430; Mexican items: ₹190-350

prose.text: Serves Indian, Italian, Mexican, Chinese, Thai and Middle Eastern dishes. Quirky decor, large servings and friendly staff.
Vegetarian, speciality is the Rajasthani thali. Credit cards are accepted and they do not serve alcohol. They also have a mithai (sweets) shop.

name: Okra
price: Appetisers, soups, salads, sandwiches, pasta, pizza, risotto: ₹225-535; Western mains: ₹575-1675; Indian and other Asian mains: ₹210-695

prose.text: Both a large buffet and à la carte. Reservations are required.

name: Zodiac
address: Fortune Park Bella Casa, Cityplex, 1, Ashram Marg, Tonk Road

prose.text: A buffet restaurant with North Indian dishes.
Upscale restaurant in the Amber Fort complex. They serve traditional Rajasthani cuisine in royally decorated dining rooms.
Northern Indian cuisine in a romantic setting, however they are reportedly a bit overpriced.

Niros is a 60-year-old restaurant serving mostly Indian and Indo-Chinese dishes. Opinions are divided between those who laud the restaurant and others who consider it overpriced and more hype than quality.
A train turned into an Italian restaurant, on the grounds of the Taj Rambagh palace. Popular among the upper class of Jaipur, they are also famous for their pizzas.

name: Virasat Heritage Restaurant
address: Delhi Road, Near Sai Baba Temple, Kukas

prose.text: Offers traditional Rajasthani and Marwari cuisine in a heritage-inspired setting and features several dining concepts, including royal-style and contemporary venues, along with facilities for weddings and other celebrations.

name: Step Out Cafe
address: P 14, Sahdev Marg, Near Secretariat, C Scheme, Ashok Nagar

prose.text: Bright and airy. Secluded garden seating. Excellent coffee. Mouth-watering desserts. Lebanese, Mexican, Italian Cuisine. Wide-rage of vegan and gluten-free options.
Mexico-themed bar at the 9th floor of the OM Tower hotel, in the adjoining room there's a dance floor. Apparently a wider range of beverages and cocktails than at restaurants.

name: Colorbar
address: Radisson Blu, Plot 5 & 6, Airport Plaza,Tonk Road, Durgapura

prose.text: On the top of the roof of Radission Blu Airport hotel, with nice views of the planes landing and taking off. Barbecue, pool and interesting luminescent chairs and tables.

name: District 9 Lounge
address: E-20, Prem Plaza, Girdhar Marg, Opposite Reliance Fresh

prose.text: Rooftop and indoor seating. More of a restaurant than a bar, with dishes from all over the world ranging from spring rolls to pizzas and fajitas to burritos.

name: Drop Zone Lounge Bar
address: 14/82 & 83, Niti Nagar, Opposite Capt Amit Bhardwaj Petrol Pump, Malviya Nagar
price: Approx ₹600 for two (without alcohol), VAT extra

prose.text: A bar with a pleasant rooftop seating with fantastic views, and they serve food as well.

name: Henry’s – The Pub
address: Park Prime Hotel, Prithviraj road, Near Statue Circle

prose.text: Cozy pub in the basement of the Prime Park Hotel, reportedly great for an evening out with your friends. Many different snacks and cocktails. On the downside some guests find the service is a bit slow.
Bar, restaurant and lounge with Mexican and Italian cuisine. Different sitting areas, which makes it a good place for private events.

name: 3D's Restro Lounge
address: A2 Corporate Tower, Near Jawahar Circle

prose.text: A lounge bar with two restaurants (fine dining and casual). A good place to hang out with your friends, and fairly popular among students.

name: Blackout
address: 9th floor, Golden Oak Hotel, Landmark Building, Ahinsa Circle, C Scheme

prose.text: Bar and nightclub popular with the party crowd, though their food is apparently not very good. Great views of the city from the rooftop lounge.

name: Club Seven
address: The Byke Grassfield Resort, Kishan Nagar

prose.text: A nightclub with electronic music and different events every few weeks at the Byke Grassfield Resort, some 6-7 km southwest of the city centre.

name: House of People
address: Hotel Las Vegas, A1, Sehkar Marg, Bais Godam

prose.text: House of People is a nightclub offering a wide variety of drinks and an amazing lounge to hang out. A pint of beer would cost about ₹250. It also attracts good gentry in general.

name: Atithi Guest House
directions: Opposite All India Radio, 2 blocks from M.I. Road
price: Standard Room: ₹1,000 single occupancy; ₹1,100 double occupancy; Large Room: ₹1,100 - 1,200 single; ₹1,200 - 1,300 double; Air-Conditioned Room: ₹1,400 single; ₹1,600 double; Extra bed: ₹350

prose.text: A nice, modern and very clean hotel a few minutes from the Pink City. Has a simple restaurant, laundry service, Wi-Fi (check on current rates, which are not posted on their site). Be careful of rickshaw/taxi drivers as they don't get a commission here so may try to bring you somewhere else.

name: Chit Chat Palace
price: Standard double with fan and hot/cold shower: ₹1,500; Family room: ₹2,000

prose.text: Airport/rail station/bus station pick up available, nice restaurant.

name: Hotel Kalyan
price: ₹850-950 for non-air-con double room; ₹1,200-2,595 for air-con double room; bigger rooms are available for up to 4 guests

prose.text: 2-star hotel with a quiet and relaxing atmosphere. Free parking and pickup is available from the train station and central bus stand. Tasty restaurant and good service.

name: Hotel Malak Mahal
price: Heritage Deluxe: ₹1,500 (double occupancy)/Negotiable; Heritage Suite: ₹2,000 (double occupancy)/Negotiable; both tariffs include taxes and breakfast

prose.text: This hotel, which opened in 2012, has 45 rooms, an in-house restaurant and reserved parking spaces. It also provides free Wi-Fi, air-con rooms with attached washrooms and a nice guest service system. Their reservation phone number is covered 24/7.

name: Hotel Pearl Palace
address: 51 Hathroi Fort, Hari Kishan Somani Marg, Ajmer Road

prose.text: The place is designed as an art museum. Wonderful roof top patio restaurant. The owners are nice but the front desk clerk is very moody. They do not always honor reservations made from their website.

name: Hotel Ramsingh Palace
address: B-2, Hathi Babu Ka Bagh, Kanti Nagar
price: Deluxe room: ₹1,700-2,200; Super Deluxe room: ₹2,000-2,500; Family Suite: ₹2800-3800; Extra bed: ₹250-500

prose.text: Comfortable beds, each room comes with LCDTV with multiple channels. Walking distance to the train station and central bus stand. Airport/rail station/bus station pick up available, multi-cuisine restaurant.

name: Hotel Sangam
price: ₹1,000 for non-air-con room; air-con rooms starting at ₹1,500

prose.text: Good mattress, TV, restaurant, includes breakfast toast.

name: Hotel Shikha
directions: 2.3 km from railway station (10 minute drive), 2.8 km from Sindhi Camp Bus Stand (10 minute drive) and 10 km from Jaipur airport (25 minute drive)

prose.text: The only hotel in Jaipur that is opposite to the deer park in c-scheme. Coffee & wine lounge in premises with Rock Pub and discotheque. Special offers on website.

name: Jaipur Inn
price: Standard Room (non-air-con): ₹1250; Deluxe Room: ₹1500; Super Deluxe Room: ₹2000; Luxury Room: ₹2950; Service Apartment (3 rooms): ₹5000

prose.text: Hot water, air-con, TV, heater, and telephone in every room. The hotel also has a backup power generator and a lift. Nice rooftop bar with great views over the city. All room rates include rooftop Wi-Fi and free cancellation. They can also serve food. During low season (April/May/June), 50% discount if you stay 2 days or more.
Good budget hotel. Very clean with hot water, quiet room. Restaurant, includes continental breakfast.

name: Moustache Jaipur
directions: 1 km from the train station, follow station road and turn right onto Mirza Ismail Rd, after 5 blocks turn left
price: 400 INR for a 12-bed dorm (no AC), private rooms and 4-bed AC rooms cost more

prose.text: Recommended by many travellers, this hostel is the headquarters of the Moustache chain. The street food tour is recommended by many. Afterwards, you can relax in the rooftop restaurant and pool.

name: Krishna Palace
price: Standard (non-air-con): ₹850 single/₹950 double; Deluxe air-con: ₹1350 single/₹1450 double; Superior air-con: ₹1500 single/₹1750 double

prose.text: Heritage property which looks like a palace. Nice garden, quiet and very clean. Traditional-style spacious rooms with private bath and hot shower. 24-hr service. Comfortable beds, each room comes with TV with all channels. Rooftop and garden restaurant available. Walking distance to the train station. Managed by a friendly family. Very quiet and relaxing neighbourhood surrounded by greenery. Pickup service from the train and central bus station is free of charge.

name: Moon Light Palace
address: S-34, Shanti Nagar, Near Labour Court

prose.text: It's clean with solid Wi-Fi. Free pick up from station. Restaurant has a wide range of food.

Clean rooms and good value with reliable hot water, TV and Wi-Fi - just ask the guy at the reception. Steps away from bus station and few min walk from old town and/or rail station. Five stores down the road south on that side of the street is an amazing vegetarian restaurant Mohal's which does great cheapish food. Make sure you get one of the rooms facing the quiet backstreet. The hotel lacks its own website, and current tariffs seem to be impossible to find online. As of 2012 or so, they charged ₹400-700 for a double room, with off season rates of ₹250 for a very basic room without attached bathroom.

name: Satkar Hotel
directions: Near railway station and bus stand

prose.text: Family run budget hotel, free pick up from railway station, bus stand, free Wi-Fi. Air-con and non-air-con rooms with attached bathrooms and TV. Hot shower, food, travel desk, laundry, 5 min walk from railway station. Not especially clean, ceiling fan noisy. Laundry is available for a charge. Walking distance to the bus station in a seedy neighbourhood.

name: Sunder Palace Guest House
price: Starting at ₹1,450 for air-con double room

prose.text: Clean rooms, great service, convenient location, a rooftop restaurant, a lovely garden area and a terrace. Tiled double room with cable TV, big bathroom with hot water and a Persian carpet area with a small table where you can sip tea and read. Internet available, but there was a charge for this service a few years ago, so enquire.

name: Siyash Luxury Girls PG
price: ₹750 Single Room, ₹550 Classic Double Room (one person), ₹600 Spacious Double Room (one person), ₹550 Triple Stay Room (one person)

prose.text: Siyash Luxury Girls PG, Jaipur – A secure and comfortable paying guest accommodation only for women. Rooms are furnished with air-conditioning, wardrobes, and study spaces. Facilities include home-style meals, Wi-Fi, 24/7 access to washing machines, housekeeping, and round-the-clock security with CCTV. Conveniently located near Kumbha Marg, which connects to the rest of the city, it is a practical option for students, working professionals, and female travellers looking for a homely stay in Jaipur.

name: Anuraag Villa
price: Starting at ₹1,650 for air-con doubles; ₹2,050 for double with garden view

prose.text: 3-star hotel 15 min by rickshaw from the city centre. Peaceful place to relax with clean, comfortable rooms and free Wi-Fi Onsite restaurant offers very good vegetarian options Rajasthani style.

name: Arya Niwas
price: Starting at ₹1,445 for an air-con double room, taxes not included. Buffet breakfast: ₹190 per person every day; buffet dinner, available only on weekends: ₹225/person.

prose.text: A feudal lord's mansion converted into a hotel with the ambience of a stately home. Centrally located, family managed, cafeteria serving decent vegetarian food and a garden to relax in during the evenings.

name: Colonel's Homestead Jaipur
address: 10 & 11 Cosmo Colony, Ram Marg, Amrapali Rd, Vaishali Nagar
price: ₹1,500/night for a double room; all rooms are air conditioned

prose.text: Run by a retired army colonel and his wife, who hails from a royal family of Rajasthan, a peaceful place to stay adjoining 50 acres of bird-filled nature. Home-cooked meals available, and good advice on attractions and shopping.

name: Hotel Classic Holidays
address: A-79, Shyam Nagar, Sodala, Ajmer Rd

prose.text: In a residential area with peaceful, clean, green surroundings.

name: Hotel Mandakini Castle
price: Double room prices as of June 2012 were ₹1,990-3,390 plus taxes. Breakfast included.

prose.text: 3-star hotel. 12 superior rooms and 26 suites. All are fitted with a private bath with hot & cold water, cable/sat TV, and broadband internet connection. The travel desk, 50-capacity conference area, complimentary transfer services. It is not easy to find current room rates, but the hotel gets mixed reviews from guests.

name: Hotel Meghniwas
address: C-9, Sawai Jai Singh Highway, Bani Park

prose.text: It also has a garden and a swimming pool, which is free for guests and open to non-guests for a charge.

name: Hotel Sarang Palace
address: A- 40, Subhash Nagar Rd, Near Peetal Factory
price: Starting at ₹1,650 for doubles without breakfast and ₹1,950 including breakfast

prose.text: 3-star heritage hotel, offers free pick up from train and bus station.

This property belongs to the Royal Family of Loharu and they rent out a few rooms. The place is quaint and beautiful and the rooms are well appointed. The service also has the touch of personal care and warmth. A plus side is the cooks are excellent and put together some fine dinners.

name: Milestone 251
address: Near Collectorate Circle, D-251, Devi Marg, Bani Park

prose.text: Near the railway station in Bani Park area.
A budget guest house.

A nicely restored heritage hotel with clean, comfortable rooms, many with balconies. Beautifully decorated, it looks like a mini-palace. It has a roof-top restaurant with views of the rising sun in the morning and the setting sun in the evening. The swimming pool is on the ground floor, and it's cold in the off-season. The friendly and helpful staff will arrange airport/train station pickup. Great value, a great place.

name: Umaid Mahal
address: C-20 / B-2, Bihari Marg, Sawai Jai Singh Highway,
directions: Opp. Lane of K.P. Automotives, Bani Park

prose.text: A very nice heritage house hotel with 3-star facilities and also offers free pick up from train and bus station.

name: Fairfield by Marriott Jaipur Tonk Road
Four Points by Sheraton Jaipur, City Square
address: City Square, Vasundhara Colony, Tonk Rd

name: ITC Rajputana, A Luxury Collection Hotel

prose.text: A luxury hotel at a walking distance from Jaipur station.

name: Lohagarh Fort Resort Jaipur
price: From ₹5,787; Airport shuttle fee: ₹2,500 per vehicle (round trip)

prose.text: 13 acres of green lush mountain area in Kukas, a 50-minute drive from Jaipur. Cottages with private pool, luxury tents with hot tub, luxury suite with hot tub. Apart from accommodation they offer spa & massage and their pool is one of the biggest in the city. They also have in-house restaurant.

Heritage home built in 1872 by the Prime Minister of Jaipur (Late Thakur Fateh Singh ji of Naila), now owned and managed by his 7th-generation descendants. It is surrounded with sprawling gardens and open spaces on all sides; the large front courtyard provides ample seating space for our visitors along with providing a calm and serine ambience. One of Jaipur's oldest heritage buildings and home the erstwhile Prime Minister, Thakur Fateh Singh Ji. Surrounded with gardens and open spaces on all sides, large front courtyard provides ample seating, antique chandeliers, original frescos, colonial furniture and a heritage of family history on display. Swimming pool, modest gym, Wi-Fi in some areas.

name: Oberoi Rajvilas Palace Hotel
price: Room prices: from ₹22,000 for a double room up to ₹500,000-750,000 for a villa with private pool. Breakfast & taxes excluded.

prose.text: If you have money to blow and you want to stay in the lap of luxury, this is the place for you. The only problem is that it is nearly impossible to get a booking.
5-star resort.

name: Taj Rambagh Palace Hotel
commons_image: Rambagh Palace hotel Jaipur lobby courtyard.jpg

prose.text: A former palace and an excellent place to stay.

name: The Trident Jaipur
price: Advance purchase rates starting at ₹5,000; otherwise, starting at ₹25,500; ₹21,000 for breakfast

prose.text: Surprisingly intimate low-rise hotel built like a glittering white Mughal palace, renovated and well maintained. Small pool. It's worth it to pay extra for a lake view room.

name: The Fern Jaipur, Series by Marriott
CKS Hospital
address: F 98 A, Road Number 6, Sikar Road, VKI

prose.text: CKS Hospital is a trusted multi-specialty hospital, open 24 hours for emergency cases.
